text.p: SabreTech Inc. said Tuesday it filed a suit against ValuJet Airlines Inc., claiming that the discount carrier is required to indemnify SabreTech for all of its damages relating to the crash of ValuJet Flight 592.
The disaster, which killed 110 people aboard a year ago, was linked to old oxygen canisters that had been incorrectly loaded into the jet's cargo.
SabreTech removed outdated oxygen generators from three MD-80 ValuJet aircraft while the aircraft were undergoing maintenance in Miami, Sabretech said.

"Following longstanding practice, the company returned ValuJet's (company materials), including tires and the generators, to ValuJet personnel who, after consultation with ValuJet's flight crew, loaded the generators on board the flight."
The company said ValuJet was unauthorised to transport the generators, which it said were identified in the airline's training manual as hazardous whether full or empty.

"For over one year, ValuJet publicly has refused to accept its responsibility for this accident and recognise its own negligence that contributed to this tragedy," said Kenneth Quinn, a spokesman for SabreTech.
"Both the FAA and SabreTech acknowledged their mistakes long ago. It's high time for ValuJet to do the same."
ValuJet officials could not be reached for comment.
The suit, filed in a federal court in Florida, alleges that ValuJet failed to provide proper oversight and guidance for its maintenance.

SabreTech, based in Phoenix, Ariz., also alleges that ValuJet failed to provide SabreTech with key letters issued by aircraft manufacturers in 1987, 1989 and 1991, or any other warnings about the hazards of oxygen generators.
SabreTech is a division of privately owned Saberliner Corp. of St. Louis.
